title: The gift: infused habits of grace and the virtues
source_text: CXLII. Hoc autem donum consistere vult in infusione habituum gratiae ac virtutum: quatenus per eos habitus mens hominis roborata elicit actum conversionis. Adeoque secundum ejus opinionem, gratia efficax aut est gratia habitualis, quum infunditur, aut ipsa ejus infusio: quatenus scilicet, per illam gratiam infusam liberum arbitrium elicit suam ipsius conversionem, Deo simul ad eam concurrente.
pass_a_gloss: CXLII. And this gift he will have consist in the infusion of habits of grace and of the virtues: inasmuch as through those habits the mind of man being strengthened elicits the act of conversion. And so according to his opinion, efficacious grace is either habitual grace, when it is infused, or its infusion itself: inasmuch namely as, through that infused grace free choice elicits its own conversion, God concurring at the same time to it.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXLII. He places this gift in the infusion of habits of grace and of the virtues, since the human mind, strengthened by those habits, elicits the act of conversion. On his view, then, efficacious grace is either habitual grace as it is infused, or the infusion itself, insofar as through that infused grace free choice elicits its own conversion, with God concurring in it at the same time.
